clue.text: Impressions of one million people — about most of nation

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other
most of a word means all but its final letter is kept

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
M is the abbreviation for million
a plain synonym
taken as written, then its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone muses on the impressions left by a single person among millions, mostly from one country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells you the people wrap round the shortened nation, rather than the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Impressions in the sense of a comic's take-offs of famous voices are mimicked performances.

clue.text: Meet Prince in trouble for cheek

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder and must be rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, including the small word in

explanation.surface: Someone meets royalty and gets into hot water for being cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' reads as a single phrase, but 'in' belongs to the letters and 'trouble' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek, as in saucy rudeness toward someone owed respect, is a common British synonym.

clue.text: Mine houses one quiet little singer

indicators.note: a building that houses something holds it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
Roman numeral one
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A small songbird is found down a mine, like a canary kept by miners.
explanation.walkthrough: I and P go together inside PIT, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipit is a small brown songbird, so a little singer describes it neatly.

clue.text: Enter with writ taken round to be edited

indicators.note: letters taken round are turned about and come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A court document is brought into a room and passed round for amendment.
explanation.definitionFit: A text that has been edited has been revised and redrafted, written over again.

clue.text: Impolite and unsatisfactory labourer

parts.note: food or service that is off is not up to standard
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A rude, shoddy worker gets a poor review.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand manner is brusque and casual, showing curt lack of courtesy.

clue.text: Cancels, including first aid books

indicators.note: including means taking inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: to annul is to cancel officially

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the opening letter of aid

explanation.surface: Someone scraps an order that included first-aid manuals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first aid' reads as one phrase, but 'first' picks a letter and 'aid' supplies it.
explanation.definitionFit: Annuals are yearbooks, children's hardback books published once each year.

clue.text: State paid a home help to come in

indicators.note: the answer comes in among the words, sitting inside them

parts.note: runs across the end of paid, all of a and the start of home

explanation.surface: Government money covers a home help who comes in to assist.
explanation.walkthrough: A home help is a carer who visits someone's house to do chores.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty United States, in the American north-west.

clue.text: Dark horse may give you a fright in bed

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: a female horse of the dark hours

definitions.text: may give you a fright in bed

explanation.walkthrough: A dark horse is normally an unexpected contender; here it is read literally, a mare of the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad dream scares a sleeper, and the word splits into the darkness and a female horse.

clue.text: Fruit father wanted to start with

parts.note: an affectionate word for father

indicators.note: to start with means only the opening letter of the preceding word is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of wanted

explanation.surface: Dad wanted fruit to begin his meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaw, or pawpaw, is a tropical fruit, another name for the papaya.

clue.text: Enthusiast gets Dan to try to dance

parts.note: a fan is a keen follower
taken as written
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: A keen friend persuades Dan to have a go at dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish courtship dance in triple time.

clue.text: Persistently loaned less in bank

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the word that follows

parts.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them
past tense of lend
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bank keeps cutting back its lending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a noun for a lender, but it is the verb, as in banking on a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something relentlessly means without pause or let-up, which is acting persistently.

clue.text: Insert new article on wine

indicators.note: a new version of a word has its letters made over into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An editor tells a magazine to add a fresh article about wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: A job taken by the French preacher

parts.note: taken as written
a post is a position of employment
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French clergyman accepts a position.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were the disciples sent out by Christ to spread his gospel, missionary preachers.

clue.text: Data fed in by noon turned up in it

indicators.note: in signals that the preceding pieces go within the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: by means next to, so two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for noon

indicators.note: turned up flips the small word so it runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then reversed

explanation.surface: Figures are entered into a computer system by midday, with IT staff showing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Data fed in' is the definition; 'by' then just means beside, joining noon to the turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is the information keyed or supplied into a computer for processing.

clue.text: Dirtying lilo put on ground

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An inflatable mattress laid on the earth gets muddy.
explanation.walkthrough: A lilo is a British inflatable air mattress for the beach or camping.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollution, the act of contaminating, is a noun for dirtying in the sense of fouling.

clue.text: Pattern on unusual tea label

parts.note: a plain synonym

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the following letters take an odd new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A decorative pattern appears on the label of an exotic tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'label' looks like a noun for a packet tag, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To designate something is to name, mark or classify it, which is to label it.

clue.text: Pompous old lady takes her medicine around one

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the medicine wraps the numeral

parts.note: a dose is a measured portion of medicine
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A self-important grandmother takes her pills one at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiose describes a showy, inflated manner, self-important and bombastic.

clue.text: For example, six-footer in queue is after Rose

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: in places the insect inside the line of waiting people

parts.note: a line of people waiting
an insect has six legs, so an ant is a six-footer

explanation.surface: An insect waiting in a queue seems to be after a girl named Rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a name or the verb, but it is the flower, capitalised to mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild European species of the rose family.

clue.text: Bury motorway being up is only temporary

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body

indicators.note: in a down light, being up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, London to Leeds, read here as MI

explanation.surface: Burying a motorway under construction is only a stopgap measure.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1, Britain's main north-south motorway, is written M-one and read as the letters MI.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim arrangement holds for the meantime until something permanent replaces it.

clue.text: Deserve to have set repaired, being zealous

parts.note: to earn something is to deserve it

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together, so these letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An eager customer feels they deserve to have their TV set fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest person is serious and intensely sincere, showing zealous conviction.

clue.text: Warning signal is changed later

indicators.note: a word that is changed has its letters altered into another order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A warning signal has been rescheduled for a later time.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is an alarm or siren sounded to warn of danger.

clue.text: Cake's half crumbled, darling

indicators.note: half means only one of the word's two halves survives

parts.note: taken as written, then its second half dropped
pet is a term of endearment

explanation.surface: Someone apologises to a loved one that the cake has partly fallen apart.
explanation.walkthrough: A crumpet is a British griddle cake, toasted and buttered; CRUM is the first four of eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumpet is a soft spongy griddle cake, so a teatime cake in British usage.

clue.text: Page behind illustration in book

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for page
behind schedule is late

explanation.surface: A page lags behind the picture in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate is a full-page printed picture, often glossy, bound into a volume.

clue.text: Shine back support in class

indicators.note: in places the preceding piece inside the word that follows

parts.note: a rate is a grade or class, as in first-rate

indicators.note: back means the following word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: aid is help or support

explanation.surface: A pupil's spinal brace makes them stand out in class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back support' reads as one medical phrase; 'back' is the signal and 'support' the word turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to give out light or heat, so to beam or shine.

clue.text: Having fool on film's an advantage

parts.note: an ass is a silly person
E.T. is Spielberg's film about an alien

explanation.surface: Casting a clown in your movie is a plus.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light, 'on' puts the fool above the film.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or resource, something that is a benefit.

clue.text: Fall out of sink in a dreadful direction

indicators.note: in a places the preceding piece inside the word that follows

parts.note: dire means terrible
to sag is to sink down
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Water spills out of a kitchen sink in a terrible way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall out of sink' reads as one phrase, but 'Fall out' is the definition and 'of' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall out with someone is to quarrel, which is to disagree in idiomatic British use.

clue.text: Get rid of job centre on American backstreet

indicators.note: centre asks for the middle letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the middle letter of job
US abbreviates United States, so American

indicators.note: back means the attached word is read in reverse

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, the word inside backstreet

explanation.surface: A job centre in a back alley of an American city sacks people.
explanation.walkthrough: A job centre is a British state employment office; here the phrase splits and 'centre' picks a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to expel or remove them from a position.

clue.text: Possibly let Tiny Tim rent from time to time

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of many possible arrangements of the following letters

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A landlord might occasionally let the Dickens child Tiny Tim rent a room.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiny Tim is the sickly boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done intermittently happens at irregular intervals, occasionally rather than continuously.
